headline: Mostly clean: EcoCard is the only card that fits, but ruling out the Crypto-Cash Back card depends on a credit-score minimum written as a dollar amount ('$660').

issues.summary: The one fact that eliminates Crypto-Cash Back for a customer with a 540 credit score is its minimum credit score, and the doc writes it as a dollar amount. Without that fact, Crypto-Cash Back would also meet every hard requirement (FTF 0%, minimum payment 1.5%, virtual cards Yes).
evidence: doc_credit_cards_crypto-cash_back_009: "What is the minimum credit score to apply for the card to earn crypto rewards? $660."
doc_credit_cards_crypto-cash_back_008: "What is the foreign transaction fee if I use the card abroad? 0%." / "What is the minimum monthly payment? 1.5% of the outstanding balance."
task_006 instructions: "You have a credit score of 540."
doc_credit_cards_ecocard_001: "Minimum credit score required to apply: 0 (0 indicates no credit score requirement)."
issues.why_it_matters: A careful agent will read '$660' as a 660 score and exclude Crypto-Cash Back, so the correct final state does not change. The corruption sits on the deciding fact, though, and an agent that dismissed it as malformed could recommend Crypto-Cash Back (which the crypto-loving customer would welcome), and the gold application would not match.
issues.suggested_fix: Change '$660.' to '660.' in doc_credit_cards_crypto-cash_back_009, and strip the '$' from the other credit-score minimums ('$640', '$680', '$720', '$750').

solution_check: Filters: FTF <= 1.5%, minimum payment <= 1.5%, virtual card management, and a score of 540. Bronze and Silver fail on FTF 2.75% and VCM 'No'. Gold requires Rho-Bank+ (he has none) and a 2.0% minimum payment. Platinum has a 2.5% minimum payment. Diamond Elite is invitation-only with a 3.0% minimum payment. Every business card needs a score of $660 or more. Crypto-Cash Back fails only on its '$660' score minimum. EcoCard passes everything (FTF 1.0%, minimum payment 1.0%, VCM Yes, score 0). That gives gold[0] apply_for_credit_card(EcoCard, Bob Nakamoto, 95000, false).
prior_note: The prior review marked this clean. The dollar-formatted score was not flagged, even though it is load-bearing here: it is the only thing excluding the crypto card.
notes: Grading model checked against the v1.0.1 snapshot: gold replay + exact agent/user DB-hash match (evaluator_env.py EnvironmentEvaluator.calculate_reward), gold-derived read-log allowlist (build.py _derive_read_log_allowlist; tools.py call_discoverable_agent_tool logs writes always, reads only if allowlisted), fixed clock (utils.get_now() = 2025-11-14 03:40, get_current_time returns '2025-11-14 03:40:00 EST') all confirmed. Numeric normalization is not global: it happens in call_discoverable_agent_tool / call_discoverable_user_tool (json parse_int=float) and inside individual tools such as apply_for_credit_card (float(annual_income)). required_documents does not list the Crypto-Cash Back docs, even though excluding that card is the core of the task. I applied one rule across my tasks: a '$'-formatted credit score is flagged Minor only where it decides the outcome (here), and goes in notes elsewhere.
